team.claim: Company leadership roster as_of 2026-10-21: Alex Bouaziz, co-founder/CEO; Shuo Wang, co-founder/CRO; Joe Kauffman, President/CFO; Dan Westgarth, COO; Philippe Bouaziz, Executive Chairman/Chief Strategy Officer; Yaron Lavi, CTO; Harish Sharma, Chief Risk Officer; DeAnn Work, General Counsel; Anthony Rodriguez, Chief Compliance Officer.
Company biographies: Alex Bouaziz previously co-founded Sarona Ventures; Shuo Wang previously co-founded Aeris Cleantec and served as CTO. Biographies accessed as_of 2026-10-21.
Company announcement: appointed Joe Kauffman President/CFO on 2025-11-03; previously CFO, President and CEO at Credit Karma. This is a CFO succession, not evidence that Philippe Bouaziz left Deel.
Company announcement: Harish Sharma joined as Chief Risk Officer in July 2025 after Pagaya; prior senior risk roles included Bank of America and HSBC North America.

TechCrunch reported that communications chief Elisabeth Diana departed in April 2025, with Deel confirming the departure. She previously worked at Instagram and Facebook; the report did not establish that litigation caused her exit.

funding.claim: Company release: $14 million Series A closed in May 2020, led by Andreessen Horowitz; disclosed as_of 2020-09-09.
Company release: $30 million Series B announced 2020-09-09, led by Spark Capital; total funding then exceeded $48 million, including seed investment.
Company release dated 2021-04-21 within a subsequently updated page: $156 million Series C led by YC Continuity Fund, at a $1.25 billion valuation; historical round as_of 2021-04-21.

Company release: $425 million Series D announced 2021-10-18, led by Coatue, at a $5.5 billion valuation; cumulative funding exceeded $630 million then. This fixes the round to its contemporaneous announcement rather than a later webpage update.

TechCrunch, citing Axios and sources, reported a $50 million financing at a $12 billion valuation involving Emerson Collective as_of 2022-05-11; press-reported, not independently confirmed here by a financing filing.

Company claim: General Catalyst and a sovereign investor purchased close to $300 million of secondary shares from early investors; reported as_of 2025-04-30. This is secondary liquidity, not equivalent primary cash raised by Deel.

Latest verified priced round as_of 2026-10-21: company announced a $300 million Series E on 2025-10-20 at a $17.3 billion valuation, co-led by Ribbit Capital, Andreessen Horowitz and Coatue. The valuation is a historical financing mark, not a current independently assessed enterprise value.

output.verdict: Deel looks commercially strong on company-reported recurring revenue growth, broad customer reach and an expanding global payroll/HR platform. Before advancing, reconcile those metrics to audited revenue and cash generation, and conduct deeper legal, governance and payment-safeguarding diligence given active Rippling litigation and the licensing/complaint evidence; allegations should not be treated as established misconduct.

business.claim: Company claim: sells a global people platform to businesses for hiring, managing and paying employees and contractors, covering payroll, HR, compliance, benefits, mobility and IT across 150+ countries; as_of 2026-10-13.

Company claim: employer-paid, per-worker monthly pricing combines software and employment services. As_of 2026-10-21, contractor management starts at $49 per contractor/month, Contractor of Record at $325 per contractor/month, US PEO at $125 per employee/month and EOR at $599 per employee/month.

Company claim: EOR includes legal employment, contracts, payroll, benefits and compliance; advertised EOR coverage is 130+ countries, distinct from broader platform reach. Pricing-page snapshot as_of 2026-10-21.

traction.claim: Company claim: 35,000 customers and 1.25 million workers as_of 2025-06-03; named customers include Reddit, Klarna and Cloudflare.
Company claim: as_of 2025-10-20, served 35,000+ customers and 1.5 million+ workers and processed $22 billion in payroll annually. Payroll volume is not Deel revenue.
Company claim: certified Workday Global Payroll Cloud partner, with expanded SAP, UKG and NetSuite integrations; Barings used Deel with Workday across 18 countries, as_of 2026-03-20.
Company claim: announced a multi-year Arsenal partnership; Arsenal became a Deel HR-platform customer as_of 2025-12-12.

Company claim: acquired AI identity-verification and deepfake-detection business Clarity; announcement called it Deel’s 15th acquisition as_of 2026-08-04. Acquisition economics were not disclosed in this release.

red_flags.claim: Active competitor litigation implicates senior executives and includes surviving RICO/trade-secret claims; prioritize discovery, governance controls, indemnities and potential damages. Based on legal_and_regulatory above, not a finding of misconduct.

Payments/licensing and worker-classification questions warrant primary-record follow-up. The Minnesota consent order is distinct from the dismissed Surge case; dismissal on standing does not resolve compliance merits. Based on legal_and_regulatory above.

Financial underwriting rests heavily on company-defined ARR/run-rate and unspecified profitability claims; obtain audited recognized revenue, margins and cash flow before relying on the historical valuation. Based on funding and financial_signals above.

Payroll/funds-access complaints concern mission-critical product functions; investigate reconciliation, safeguarding, support SLAs and loss history rather than extrapolating BBB allegations to all customers. Based on reputation above.

reputation.claim: Employee-review aggregator Glassdoor snapshot as_of 2026-10-21: 4.3/5 across 2,132 reviews and 83% recommendation rate. Compensation/benefits was 4.0/5; the page reported that rating down 6% over the preceding 12 months. Anonymous, self-selected reviews are not a representative employee survey.

Glassdoor reviews accessed 2026-10-21 praise remote flexibility, autonomy and learning while recurring criticisms concern intense pace, compensation/progression and work-life sustainability; individual employee opinions, not adjudicated company-wide facts.

Customer-complaint aggregator BBB snapshot as_of 2026-10-21: 17 complaints over the prior three years and eight closed over the prior 12 months. Displayed complaints concern billing, payroll/funds access, withdrawals and support; BBB does not independently verify allegations, and the sample does not establish an incidence rate.
Critical press: TechCrunch described the Rippling espionage allegations and Deel’s denial of wrongdoing. Coverage creates reputational exposure; it does not establish liability.

financial_signals.claim: Company claim, latest opened financial update: exceeded $1.5 billion ARR in H1 2026 and described continued profitable growth. Announcement dated 2026-08-04; ARR is not audited annual recognized revenue.

Company claim: $1 billion annual revenue run-rate and 75% year-on-year revenue growth as_of 2025-06-03; profitable for nearly three years. These are management statements, not audited financial statements.

Company claim: exceeded $1 billion ARR earlier in 2025, reached its first $100 million revenue month in September 2025 and reported three consecutive years of profitability as_of October 2025. Profitability basis was not specified in this release.
Company claim: 6,500+ team members across 100+ countries as_of 2025-06-03. This is a dated workforce snapshot, not a verified October 2026 employee count.

CNBC reported approximately 5,000 employees as_of 2025-02-04; compared with the later company-reported 6,500+ team members in June 2025, this suggests expansion but is not a like-for-like audited headcount series.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: Rippling litigation: People Center, Inc. v. Deel, Inc., N.D. Cal. 3:25-cv-02576-CRB, filed 2025-03-17. Official docket shows active discovery/status proceedings and filings through 2026-10-14; no final liability finding is established by the opened docket.

Court order dated 2026-02-23: Rippling alleges corporate espionage and trade-secret theft involving Deel and executives. The court denied dismissal of the RICO and federal trade-secret claims while dismissing certain state-law claims; pleading-stage survival is not proof of misconduct.

Surge receiver complaint filed 2025-01-03 alleged unlicensed money transmission, AML/KYC/OFAC-control failures and sanctions-related payment exposure involving Deel. These are plaintiff allegations, not a regulator finding or criminal conviction.

Damian v. Deel, Inc., S.D. Fla. 1:25-cv-20017: court dismissed the Surge receiver action and closed the case on 2025-08-18 for lack of Article III standing. The ruling does not adjudicate the underlying allegations true.

The Surge complaint reproduces a Minnesota Commerce consent order dated 2024-05-23 concerning alleged unlicensed cash-advance/lending and money-transmission activity. Source is an exhibited regulatory document hosted with plaintiff counsel, not a directly retrieved regulator record; complete terms, penalty and subsequent compliance remain unverified.

California Senator Steve Padilla requested a labor-agency investigation on 2023-07-06, alleging misclassification of Deel’s own workers and problematic client advice. This is a legislative referral, not an agency adjudication; subsequent disposition was not verified.

input: Write a due diligence memo on Deel
